relevance_note: The paper describes four children with heterozygous TNFAIP3 variants or deletion, each with individual clinical and genetic detail: 'Genetic testing identified TNFAIP3 mutations in all four patients'.
method_note: Read the full paper manually; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and copied table spans directly from the Markdown rows of Tables 1-3 (patients are columns, headers 'Patient 1' to 'Patient 4'); every transcribed cell value was checked against the tables by eye and every span checked verbatim by script. Scope: the four patients plus both parents of Patients 1, 3 and 4, who are described as tested wild-type (labelled 'parent of Patient k' and 'parent of Patient k 2', because the paper writes only 'parents', never mother/father). Patient 2's parents are not described (only Table 3 'de novo'), so they get no rows. Table 1 legend defines '−' as 'Negative'; Table 2 legend defines '−' as 'Normal' (used as negative for the autoantibody panel, gastroscopy, brain MRI, EMG, bone marrow aspiration); '/' (not done) is treated as not reported. The paper uses 'aphthosis' interchangeably with ulcer (e.g. 'gastric aphthosis' vs Table 2 'Gastric ulcer'), so Oral/Genital aphthosis map to the oral/genital ulcer checklist items. 'Arthritis −' was not used to exclude 'arthritis or arthralgia'. 'Skin eruption −' was used to exclude the skin-lesion item (the paper counts erythema nodosum as a skin eruption). 'Hepatic injury −' was used to exclude autoimmune hepatitis (Patients 1-3). Numeric values that the authors do not interpret (ALB, LDH, NE, CCP, ASO) and tests that are not phenotypes (pathogen screening, skin prick test) were not recorded as features. Patient 1's persisting intermittent fever and perianal aphthosis come from the abstract's '1 patient ... with IFX and azathioprine', who is Patient 1 (the only patient given IFX and azathioprine). Patient 2 inheritance 'de novo' rests on Table 3 plus the methods statement that first-degree relatives were sequenced; the text's parental-testing sentence names only the three SNVs. is_proband for Patients 2-4 rests on the methods phrase 'the proband’s phenotype'. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the c.133C > T variant is 'previously reported [5, 6]' but the paper does not say Patient 3 was described before. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) Patient 4 cDNA is c.1243_1247del in the abstract, results text, Fig. 4 legend and ACMG sentence but c.1247_1251del in Table 3; the text form was recorded. (2) 'Patients 1, 3, and 4 carried novel frameshift or nonsense mutations' vs Patient 3's variant 'has been previously reported [5, 6]'. (3) Text says 'rheumatoid factor ... were negative' but Table 2 gives 'RF-IgA elevated' for Patients 1, 2 and 4; the RF-IgA rows were kept and the autoantibody checklist item set to not reported for those three. (4) Abstract: 'lymphadenopathy in one case' vs lymph node enlargement in both Patient 1 (CT, Fig. 1B) and Patient 4 (ultrasound). (5) Abstract lists arthritis among features 'in 50% of patients' but Table 1 shows arthritis only in Patient 2. (6) Discussion: 'T/B lymphopenia in Patients 1 and 2' vs Table 2 'CD8 + T cells increased' for Patient 1. (7) Patient 2's deletion is called heterozygous, yet the discussion says 'complete A20 deficiency'/'complete A20 loss'. (8) 'intestinal mucosal edema in all patients (4/4)' although Table 2 lists only knee findings for Patient 2's ultrasound (Patient 2's edema recorded as inferred from group statement). (9) Patient 3 ESR 19 is within the printed reference (0–20) and Patient 4 HGB 110 equals the lower reference limit, yet the text says all had elevated inflammatory markers and anemia (Patient 4 anemia recorded as inferred from group statement). (10) Table 3 domain for Patient 4 is 'ZnF1' but the text places the variant 'between the ZnF1 and ZnF2 domains'. (11) Patient 2's knee MRI findings sit in the Table 2 row labelled 'Abdominal MRI'.
